newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Kalimantan hit by campaign rioting.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Kalimantan hit by campaign rioting.

text.p: Rioters set ablaze a major hotel and attacked churches in the town of Banjarmasin in Indonesia's South Kalimantan province on Friday after clashes between rival political groups, residents said on Saturday.

Fighting between supporters of the ruling Golkar party and the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) on the last day of campaigning for next Thursday's general election spilled over into widespread violence.
Church sources said at least seven churches were either burnt, looted or stoned.

"Only one church was burnt, but all the churches in Banjarmasin suffered severe damage with all their possessions looted and the buildings stoned," one priest, who asked not to be named, told Reuters. He added he had just come out of hiding.
Jakarta was quiet on Saturday, the first day of a "cooling off" period before next Thursday's elections.
The Kompas newspaper said a number of Golkar offices were either burnt or damaged in Friday's rioting and reported extensive damage to shops after they were stoned.
It said the four-star Hotel Kalimantan as well as a supermarket and a cinema were burnt.
"The damage is extraordinary," one resident told Reuters.
The official Antara news agency said 32 people had been treated for knife wounds, cuts and burns. Residents said at least two people were killed but there was no immediate confirmation.

Residents said troops had been flown into Banjarmasin, a city of 400,000 on the Indonesian half of Borneo island, and that the situation was now calm and under control, although all shops and offices remained closed.
"Nothing is open. There are troops throughout the city," the resident said.

Police declined to comment on the riot but said the situation in Banjarmasin on Saturday was calm. There have been widespread clashes between PPP and Golkar supporters on the main Java island, but little property damage.
Kompas newspaper said the fighting started after Golkar loyalists began campaigning before Friday Islamic prayers, enraging people going to mosques, many of whom were PPP supporters.
The clashes then deteriorated into widespread rioting, it said.
The paper quoted armed forces spokesman Brigadier-General Slamet Supriadi as saying the violence was purely criminal.
"This is an immoral action which exceeds the limits of the nation's tolerance. We will take firm action against those who did this," Supriadi said.
"Military headquarters greatly regrets an incident like this in a nation which is struggling for a democratic life," he said.

The last day of the campaign was marked by a number of clashes in south and central Jakarta as well as the outlying satellite cities of Bekasi and Tangerang. Kompas said there were also disturbances in Bangil, East Java, and that three churches were stoned.

Golkar, the PPP and the Indonesian Democratic Party are the three parties entitled to contest the elections, in which 425 members of the national parliament will be chosen as well as legislators for the provincial and district bodies.
